title: Choose colour policy for redirected console output
goal: Request ANSI colour for a piped Unix console application, or disable it without changing persistent environment settings.

selectionNotes: FORCE_COLOR enables the verified Unix route. Windows redirected Console emitted no ANSI; macOS execution is unverified.
Not tested: macOS execution: no Mac environment. Excluded under PIN-699; recorded Windows/Linux results remain separate.

runtime.name: .NET
runtime.reason: This edition uses .NET 11 library APIs; the .NET 10 code is a comparison, not a catalogue route.

sdk.name: .NET SDK
sdk.reason: Build the declared net11.0 sample with the .NET 11 SDK.

language.name: C#
language.reason: The canonical net11.0 project selects the .NET 11 default C# 15 language mode.

platforms: macOS (native execution not tested); Windows checked without ANSI support
prerequisites: Use a net11.0 console project with LangVersion=15.0. Include the imports stated in the recipe.
constraints: The exercised Linux route uses TERM=xterm-256color and Console.ForegroundColor/ResetColor with stdout redirected. Windows RC2 execution emitted no ANSI in either mode: this recipe does not claim FORCE_COLOR enables Windows redirected Console colouring. macOS follows the Unix implementation but has no native execution proof here. Other logging libraries and tools may interpret these conventions differently. FORCE_COLOR does not change IsOutputRedirected or guarantee renderer support. Child-local Environment entries do not mutate the parent, user or machine environment.
stabilityLimitations: RC2 verification; GA reconciliation remains pending.
